findings.claim: Immediate selection evidence is only weakly aligned with descendant credit: the compressed-choice excess fixed-frame RMS is small (whole-window mean ~0.081 A, CI95 ~0.070-0.092) and top-4 teacher overlap is ~0.47, so the chosen candidate is often not the nearest teacher. Chosen-teacher score correlations are near zero (compressed ~0.10, full ~0.064), indicating selection evidence does not strongly predict later quality credit.

The actual later-label calculation is terminal-credit mining over survival moments with BH correction jointly over 400 survival field/measure tests, explicitly not terminal affinity effects. Ancestral coverage is thin: 349 of 700 batch nodes have fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 have fewer than 6, with at most 2 teachers per batch, so survivor bias and sparse ancestry limit any last-record credit interpretation.

Decoded terminal labels are unavailable: terminal metadata show only a single future-resampling node per batch at terminal index 99 (score time 0.99, state time 1.0), and the label semantics state recorded affinities were removed with an equal score prior. Therefore last-record credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit; the immediate-selection versus descendant-quality comparison is unavailable.

Among endpoint coordinate effects, shape descriptors carry the strongest and most reproducible signal: shape_yy has integrated z ~ -0.51 with 0.0 positive batch fraction (q ~ 1.5e-5) and shape_xx ~ -0.50 (q ~ 8e-4), while global_centroid_y is weaker (~ -0.24, q ~ 0.014) and centroid_x/z are not significant. This differs from ranking point estimates alone, which would not separate these by multiplicity-adjusted support and batch agreement.

Curve support is restricted: only 24 of 200 continuous features pass the selection rule (|integrated z| >= 0.1, batch direction fraction >= 0.857, q < 0.05, scale floor excluded) with a fidelity rule of relative RMSE <= 0.35 and zero strong sign conflicts. The fidelity audit is delivered as a container summary only, so per-feature sign changes and rate changes are not yet read.

hypotheses.direction: increase weight on shape-coupled landmark contrast relative to constant global-centroid terms
hypotheses.falsifier: no validated fit or observed-node interpolation for the shape-coupled contrast, or sign conflicts exceeding the fidelity rule
hypotheses.observable: validated absolute contrast change at observed score nodes for shape-coupled landmark features
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned regional attention rule that modulates landmark occupancy/softmin contrast at observed score nodes may express the shape-driven endpoint signal better than a constant rule, because the strongest reproducible endpoint effects are shape descriptors rather than centroid translation.

hypotheses.direction: retain freedom in surrounding coordinates while steering shape-coupled regions
hypotheses.falsifier: an independent batch showing opposite sign for shape_yy/shape_xx, or a joint diagnostic attributing the effect to common motion
hypotheses.observable: integrated z and positive batch fraction for shape versus centroid features
hypotheses.statement: Prioritizing shape_yy/shape_xx over global_centroid_y for coordinate control is supported by multiplicity-adjusted support and batch agreement, but remains a coordinate contrast hypothesis, not an affinity target.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels are supplied; last-record survival credit cannot be interpreted as final affinity benefit.
The curve fidelity audit is a container summary only; per-feature sign changes and rate changes were not read.
Endpoint and increment effects are coordinate contrasts, not physical interaction energies or evidence of neural-module causation.
Turnover residual and survival moments are accounting diagnostics, not causal selection effects or atom velocities.
